title: Budgeted shard architecture & hot-path prioritization for audit ingest
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: design and implement a cost-predictable audit ingestion storage layout that prioritizes hot-path events (RBAC changes, admin actions, SSO/SAML auth failures) for low-latency query while ensuring long-tail events are compacted into cold storage with automated retention and cost caps. This ticket covers the ingestion throttling/priority layer, tenant-aware shard budgeting, index lifecycle policies (hot->warm->cold->archive), and the operational controls for capping quarterly storage spend. Work traces the ingestion pipeline (kinesis/fluentd -> processing -> enrichment -> primary index and cold-object store) and defines a hands-off autoscaling and cap-fallback policy for tenants that exceed budgets.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Ingest path accepts prioritized events and routes to hot shards with >95th percentile write latency <200ms under 90th percentile load.
2) Tenant budget config API exists and is enforced; tenants hitting budget are rate-limited and non-critical events are demoted to cold store.
3) Index lifecycle policies implemented: hot (7d), warm (30d), cold (90d), archive (365d) with configurable per-tenant overrides.
4) Cost controls: nightly cost estimation job and automatic shard throttling when expected 7-day spend > budget.
5) Dashboards (Grafana) and alerts for ingestion lag, hot shard utilization, and unexpected cost spikes are live.
6) Migration/rollout plan and runbook published in Confluence and reviewed by Security and SRE.
tasks: Design tenant-aware shard budgeting model (docs: Confluence link)
Add event priority field at producer and propagate through pipeline
Implement hot-path routing in ingestion service (service PR: platform/pull/5678)
Index lifecycle policy templates and per-tenant overrides in provisioning API
Nightly cost estimator job that projects 7-day spend and emits cost_limit_exceeded metric
Rate-limit/demotion controller that triggers when projected spend > budget
Create Grafana dashboards and alerts, link to incident runbook
E2E tests for priority routing and cold-store retrieval latency
comments: 2026-01-28 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after architecture sync with Security and SRE. We need to make retention configurable per-tenant and tie RBAC-sensitive events (admin, role changes) to stricter hot retention by default. See design stub: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/Audit+Ingest+Sharding+Draft

2026-02-02 Diego Alvarez: Spike complete. Two candidate shard models evaluated: (A) tenant-first shards (one or more shards dedicated per high-volume tenant) and (B) time-first shards with tenant hashing. Trade-off: tenant-first gives predictable per-tenant costs but more waste for low-QPS tenants; time-first is simpler for cross-tenant queries. Recommendation: hybrid — high-volume tenants get budgeted shards; all others use hashed time-based shards.

2026-02-10 SRE Review (Priya Rao): Concern about hot shard hotspots when a tenant bursts. Proposed mitigation: short-term autoscale + token-bucket per-tenant write limiter and fallback demotion to cold path. Also suggested adding backpressure signals into producers. See comments in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5678

2026-02-18 Security Review (Lars M.): Approve default hot retention for RBAC/SAML auth-fail events (30d hot instead of 7d) but require opt-out guardrails. Flagged data classification coupling — need metadata flag on events marking PII or sensitive, which affects retention and encryption at rest configuration.
